items.title: Lorraine Feather interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, March 22, 2023
items.q: Milt Hinton, the bassist, talking about recording sessions with Dinah Washington

ctx.x: The recordings I’ve listened to are — I’ll relate another thing I remember reading. Milt Hinton, the bassist, talking about recording sessions with Dinah Washington and the quartet would get there ahead of time and sort of run through the tunes and then she’d walk in and say, “Okay what have we got?” And she would do one take and consider it done. So this long intro to my question is how do your arrangements occur, which are quite precise at times?

Well the composers are the arrangers and some of what they do is very precise and meant to be played as written. And then there are other spots that are left loose because they know the personality of the people who are going to be on the session in most cases. And they want that person to be able to play a little solo or to do something that has a certain vibe but they don’t dictate exactly what it is.
